intro: Singapore is a tiny island city-state that grew from a British trading post into one of the richest places on Earth in a single lifetime.

chapters.title: Temasek
text: In the 1300s a trading town called Temasek stood here. According to legend, a prince named it Singapura, 'Lion City', after seeing a lion-like animal.

chapters.title: British Singapore
text: In 1819 Stamford Raffles set up a British trading post. As a free port on the Strait of Malacca, Singapore boomed, attracting Chinese, Malay and Indian migrants.
Japan captured Singapore in 1942, Britain's worst military defeat, and occupied it until 1945.

highlight.title: Fall of Singapore
highlight.text: Winston Churchill called the 1942 surrender the worst disaster in British military history.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Singapore joined Malaysia in 1963 but was expelled in 1965 and became independent. Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew, in power until 1990, built housing, industry and a strong state.
With no natural resources, it relied on trade, education and attracting foreign companies.

timeline.title: Raffles
timeline.text: A British trading post is founded.

timeline.title: Self-government
timeline.text: Lee Kuan Yew becomes prime minister.

timeline.title: SG50
timeline.text: Fifty years of independence; Lee Kuan Yew dies.

keyTerms.meaning: A country made up of one city.
A port where goods can be traded without import taxes.
